newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power falls for Monday ahead of warming.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power falls for Monday ahead of warming.

text.p: Spot bulk power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) fell on Friday for Monday delivery with a warming trend forecast for the next several days in the state, industry sources said.
Temperatures in Texas were expected to be five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit below normal Saturday, but were called to return to normal and above normal levels by early next week.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Monday delivery was discussed at $25.00-29.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) from $54.00-59.00 for next day power on Thursday, the brokers and marketers said.
Early in the day some spot ERCOT power for Monday delivery had been talked higher, with one unconfirmed peak trade reported at $34.00 per MWh.
ERCOT non-firm peak power was notionally pegged at $23.00-25.00 from $47.00-52.00 on Thursday, the sources said.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Monday were notionally assessed at $15.00-19.00 from $29.00-31.00 in Thursday discussion.
February ERCOT peak power was said to have declined behind continued lower natural gas prices, wth talk at $30.00-31.75 from $31.50-33.50 on Thursday.
South Texas spot natural gas prices were said to have declined by about $1.00 on Friday to near $3.70 per million British thermal units.
